conviction_note: Findings offset: base-oil posted increases after the Aug 5 call (Motiva +$1.00/gal Group III Sep 1, SK Enmove +$0.50 Sep 8, record Group III prices in October with Gulf supply still stranded) press the quarter and the first FY27 guide, against a Brent collapse in early November on US-Iran peace hopes, an accelerating closest-peer comp (Take 5 +4.9% vs +3.6%), an RBC-lowered bar for the FY27 guide and ~11% of float short; impact_sum +0.20 and the scaled number -0.12 (p_up 49 x abs 6.0) agree on 'near zero', and the abs move is set above the 4.98% median because this print carries the first FY27 guide.
bar: Q4 FY26 consensus adj EPS $0.42 and revenue $566.7M (Earnings Whispers preview via finviz, 2026-11-11, https://finviz.com/news/421321/valvoline-heads-into-fiscal-q4-with-sales-booming-but-base-oil-costs-squeezing-margins); FY26 company guide adj EPS $1.70-1.75, adj EBITDA $550-560M, net revenue $2.05-2.10B, SSS 7.5-8%, Q4 EBITDA margin -300 to -400 bp implied (Q3 call 2026-08-05, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/valvoline-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-09/); FY26 street EPS $1.75-1.78 sits at the TOP of guide (chartmill 1.78 on 2026-10-24, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/VVV/estimates) while revenue sits at the bottom. FY27 consensus EPS ~$1.97-1.98 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/vvv/forecast/, down ~4.6% over 90 days per tickzen). Bar sourced to a company guide plus two estimate sources that agree within rounding; print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest 14,150,675 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, 5.81 days to cover (14.66M / 5.21 on 10-15; 15.44M / 4.53 on 09-30) per https://equibles.com/stocks/vvv/shortinterest, roughly 11% of float (Equibles put 13.1M at 10.3% of float). Moderately crowded, not extreme. No usable option skew: front expiry 2026-11-20 chain is unusable (ATM spread 165% of mid, 138 contracts OI, put/call OI 0.23); ATM IV 128% on 2 DTE would imply ~9.5% but is not tradable information. Tape: -6.57% over 5 days into the print after a rebound from a post-August low of $26.21 to $35.73 on 2026-11-11; +7.78% over 20 days; 16.7% below the 52w high.

findings.finding: Base-oil cost pressure intensified AFTER Valvoline last spoke on 2026-08-05: Motiva raised Group II+/III posted prices $1.00/gal effective Sep 1 and SK Enmove +$0.50/gal effective Sep 8, with Persian Gulf base-oil shipments still cut off and Bahrain/Qatar/Abu Dhabi production shut (Lubes'n'Greases, 2026-09-02 and 09-09), and Argus on 2026-10-08 reported record-high Group III prices persisting; against a Q4 EPS consensus of $0.42 that already sits at the top of the $1.70-1.75 FY guide and management's statement that price and cost would be back in balance by quarter-end, this points to the low end of the Q4 EBITDA margin guide (-300 to -400 bp) and to a FY27 first half still under cost pressure versus a FY27 EPS consensus of ~$1.97.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-05 the base-oil margin warning (with a raised comp guide and an EPS beat) took the stock -5.86% close to close (opened $36.40 vs $39.28 prior close); the prior Q4 print with the first annual guide (2025-11-19) went -2.48%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the base-oil shock is the known story and the stock fell 5.9% on it in August. What is not visibly in the price is the size of the post-call September increases (they are in a trade-press price report, not in any VVV preview), and the stock rallied ~36% off its low into 2026-11-11 on falling crude, which would not happen if the market were pricing record Group III costs flowing into FY27 H1. If this were fully priced the Street would sit at or below the guide midpoint for Q4 rather than at the top, and FY27 EPS would have been cut more than ~4.6% in 90 days.
findings.independence: Argus Media, 2026-10-08, record-high Group III prices with Mideast Gulf supply (~20% of global Group III, 47% of US Group III imports in 2025) still stranded: https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/market-opinion-and-analysis-blog/european-base-oils-group-iii-price-pressure ; Lubes'n'Greases 2026-09-02 (same publisher, same Motiva increase): https://www.lubesngreases.com/?p=215911 . Industry posted prices are a proxy for VVV's finished-lubricant cost; the company buys finished product, so transmission lag and contract terms are not confirmed by the company.

findings.finding: Crude collapsed in early November on US-Iran peace hopes: Brent fell about 16% in the week to 2026-11-09 (sharpest weekly drop since 2020) with JPMorgan citing a ~1.4 mb/d October surplus, and fell another ~2.5% in the week to 2026-11-13; management said on the Q3 call that the industry historically does not roll back prices when lubricant costs fall and that it expects margin-rate expansion toward historical patterns as costs moderate, which gives the first FY27 guide a credible back-half margin recovery path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on cost relief; the stock's rebound from $26.21 to $35.73 between August and 2026-11-11 coincided with the crude decline, then gave back 6.6% in the five sessions before the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced in the rally to $35.73; what remains is whether management converts it into a guide that includes H2 FY27 margin expansion. The 5-day -6.6% drawdown into the print suggests the market has partly given the relief back; if it were fully priced the stock would be at or above the Nov 11 high.
findings.independence: Brent losses after Nov 9 settlement: https://www.nationthailand.com/news/world/40073309 ; management's price-stickiness comment is from the Q3 call summary https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/valvoline-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-09/ . Crude is a weak proxy for Group III, which stayed physically tight (finding 1), and the preview says management warned costs could stay elevated 4-6 months after the Strait reopens.

findings.finding: Closest peer Take 5 (Driven Brands) reported preliminary same-store sales of +4.9% for the quarter ended 2026-09-26, accelerating from +3.6% in Q2, with 27 net new units; the same release cut Driven's FY26 outlook (Take 5 SSS now 3.5-4.0%, EBITDA $410-430M from $430-460M) citing pressure on lower-income consumers. This covers the same calendar months as VVV's fiscal Q4 (Jul-Sep) and landed after VVV last spoke, consistent with price pass-through holding ticket while traffic softens.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: VVV's comp line: Q3 FY26 comp +8% (three-quarters ticket) with a raised comp guide; the stock still fell 5.86% on the margin warning, so comp strength alone has not been paid when margins disappoint.
findings.why_not_priced: Driven's release was dominated by its restatement and delayed 10-Q, so the Take 5 comp acceleration got little read-across coverage; the VVV preview of 2026-11-11 does not mention it. Revenue consensus sitting at the bottom of VVV's guided range is what you would not see if the market were reading Take 5's acceleration as a pass-through tell. The lower-income comment cuts the other way and is netted into the size.
findings.independence: Driven Q2 2026 8-K with Take 5 +3.6%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001804745/000180474526000072/q22026earningsrelease.htm . One document carries both the acceleration and the consumer warning; counted once.

findings.finding: RBC Capital on 2026-10-21 cut its target to $46 from $49 (Outperform) and said it expects Valvoline's initial FY27 guidance to be 'fairly conservative', a published expectation that lowers the bar the first FY27 guide must clear.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First annual guides: 2025-11-19 -2.48% (analysts cut targets after), 2024-11 not in the sealed history; mixed.
findings.why_not_priced: It is wire copy, so mostly priced; filed small because it sets expectations for a conservative guide that FY27 consensus (~$1.97) may not fully reflect.

findings.finding: Valvoline priced $600M of 6.125% senior notes due 2034 (upsized from $500M) on 2026-08-13, closed 2026-08-24, to repay term loan A in full and part of term loan B, terming out floating debt at a fixed coupon that likely lifts FY27 interest expense slightly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three months; what is not yet visible is the FY27 interest line in the guide. What the money buys: a refinancing of acquisition-era term loans (Breeze), not distress and not a ramp, so near zero.

findings.finding: Short interest stood at 14.15M shares (~11% of float), 5.81 days to cover at the 2026-10-30 settlement, and the stock fell 6.57% in the five sessions into the print, so a guide that is merely in line carries squeeze potential.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Up moves of +6.94% (2026-02-04) and +7.44% (2025-02-06) show the name can rip on relief; no squeeze attribution sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public but the 5-day drawdown means positioning got more defensive into the print; a market that had covered would show the stock near the Nov 11 high and falling days to cover.
findings.independence: Equibles summary (10.3% of float at 2026-09-30): https://equibles.com/stocks/vvv/summary

findings.finding: US vehicle travel turned negative year on year in May 2026 (-0.7% to 293.2bn miles, first decline since Feb 2025) as gasoline hit a four-year high of $4.56/gal; with Brent above $100 again in September, miles driven is a proxy headwind for oil-change transaction counts in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a line VVV has traded on; transaction softness among lower-income households was flagged on the Q3 call.

findings.why_not_priced: Macro proxy, months old and not confirmed for Jul-Sep; Take 5's comp acceleration in the same months (finding 3) says the effect on the oil-change channel is small, so sized small.

baseline_tension: No usable skew; the evidence splits between post-call cost escalation (negative, partly priced by the August -5.9%) and a November crude collapse plus an accelerating peer comp and a moderately crowded short (positive), which matches a stock that ran 36% off its low and then gave back 6.6% into the print.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): ~11% of float short with 5.8 days to cover, so the base-oil finding moved from -1.2 to -1.0 and p_up from 48 to 49.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the notes refinance acquisition term loans, so the financing finding stays near zero (-0.1) rather than read as distress.
Rule 5 (proxy vs broader series): the VMT proxy stays small (-0.2) because the direct peer's comp in the same months points the other way; kept, not dropped.
Rule 3 / one-document rule: the Take 5 acceleration and its lower-income warning stay one finding, netted.
